utility.notes: Directly confirmed via Xcel Energy's own Colorado customer portal. Xcel Energy is Colorado's largest electric utility, dominant across the Front Range/Denver metro.

value.name: Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Denver this session; Xcel Energy is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Denver is a consolidated city-county government (City and County of Denver) — one of only a few in the U.S.

permit_authority.value: City and County of Denver, Community Planning and Development (CPD)
permit_authority.notes: Denver is NOT part of Colorado's State Electrical Board 'state inspected areas' — Denver is explicitly named on DORA's own 'Electrical Local Inspection Areas' list, meaning the City itself (not the state) is the electrical permitting/inspection authority here, in addition to its own building permit authority. This is the opposite arrangement from the ~200+ smaller/rural Colorado jurisdictions that rely on DORA's State Electrical Board — see the state-level note in this record's notes/sources for the correct, non-overgeneralized scope of that state program.

interconnection_url.notes: Xcel Energy's own Colorado Net Energy Metering page. All solar customers receive net energy metering; excess generation is banked against future bills. Eligibility requires an active Xcel Energy account, UL 1741 SB-certified equipment, and (for larger systems) general liability insurance — no insurance requirement applies below 1 MW AC, so this does not affect typical residential systems.

battery_programs.notes: Xcel Energy's own page references a 'Solar*Rewards' incentivized REC-payment program as a separate track from net metering, but this session did not independently verify whether it includes a battery/storage-specific component or dollar figures — left null rather than guessed.

value: A qualified person (licensed master/journeyman electrician, residential wireman, or — for systems with 400A service or less — a NABCEP-certified solar installer capable of testing rapid shutdown) must be present at the PV electrical inspection
If structural enhancements are required (beyond blocking/sistering of rafters, joists, or truss top chords), a rough framing inspection must also be requested
At inspection, the contractor must submit written documentation that grounding/bonding was performed per NEC 690.41-690.47 and all roof-mounted equipment complies with NEC guidelines
The rapid shutdown system must be tested at the final electrical inspection with the inspector present

timeline_days.notes: No explicit day-count review/inspection timeline was found on the City's own solar-permit or building-permit-policy pages this session. The 'Average Plan Review Times' dashboard page exists but renders as an embedded interactive dashboard, not extractable static text; the Xcel Energy interconnection process guide PDF also could not be read (image-based).

value.program_or_pathway: SolarApp+ Quick Permit (Electrical) for eligible single-family/duplex projects; standard electrical + building permit review otherwise
other_conditions: SolarApp+ eligibility: single-family or duplex home, utility service of 400A or less, DC rating under 10kW, no service upgrades/new AC panels/EV chargers/home rewiring/solar shingles in scope
A zoning permit is required first if panels are not flush-mounted, or if a generator/energy storage system will be located on the exterior of the structure
A Certificate of Appropriateness from Landmark Preservation is required first if the property is in a historic district or a designated landmark
Engineered plans with a PE seal are not required for 1-2 family homes/townhomes unless the system is 10kW or more, or includes a generator or solar shingles
Roof access/pathway requirements apply: two 36-inch-wide access pathways on separate roof slopes, at least one on the street/driveway side; ridge setbacks of 18-36 inches depending on roof coverage

value.name: Solar Photovoltaic (PV) and other renewable energy building permit fee (flat, replaces the standard valuation-based fee)
value.unit: flat fee per permit (including each subsequent modified permit for PV-related scope)
value.notes: Applies to both single-family residential and commercial PV installations. Where non-solar work is also part of the project, this flat fee applies only to the solar PV portion; non-PV work is billed at the standard valuation-based rate.

value.name: Plan review fee for PV or other renewable energy system permits
value.notes: The standard plan review fee (normally 50% of the permit fee) is $0 for PV/renewable-energy permits.

permit_fees.notes: Directly extracted from the City's own 'Building and Related Fees' policy (ADMIN 125/138, revised May 21, 2024), Table 1's 'Special Fee Modifications — Fee Reductions' row, which is explicitly and unambiguously labeled 'Solar Photovoltaic (PV) and other renewable energy (RE) projects' — not a general fee cap or an unrelated category.

value.name: Colorado Residential Solar Property Tax Exemption
value.administrator: Colorado Division of Property Taxation (Dept. of Local Affairs)
value.description: Statewide Colorado property tax exemption: independently owned residential solar electric generation facilities (photovoltaic systems) meeting the criteria in §39-1-102(6.8), C.R.S. are exempt from Colorado property taxation under §39-3-102, C.R.S. To qualify, the facility must be located on residential real property, used to produce electricity primarily for use in the residential improvements, and have a production capacity of no more than 100 kW AC. This is a genuine statewide exemption applicable to any qualifying Colorado residential system, not utility- or city-specific — distinct from any local (county/municipal) incentive, which the Division's own page notes Colorado does NOT offer at the general statewide level (only county/municipal governments may separately opt to offer their own local property/sales tax credits under §§30-11-107.3 and 31-20-101.3, C.R.S.).
value.eligibility: Residential real property, system owned by the residential property owner, electricity used primarily for the residential improvements, production capacity ≤100 kW AC.

rebates.notes: Verified directly from the Colorado Division of Property Taxation's own official page. Xcel Energy's own page separately references a 'Solar*Rewards' incentivized REC-payment program, but no dollar figure or rate for that separate program was independently confirmed this session.
